Here's a regex that matches an ISO 8601 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` is the four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` is the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` is the day, 01–31.
- `^` and `$` anchor the match to the whole string. To find dates inside longer text, replace them with `\b`.

It matches `2026-10-01`. It doesn't check that the day exists in that month, so `2026-02-31` also passes. Leap years and month lengths need code logic or a date parser on top of the regex.
